title: Cisco Secure Malware Analytics Submission Volume
exclusions: Counts sandbox submissions. The add-on publishes no threat-score field, so malicious and benign samples are not separated.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Submit a test sample to Secure Malware Analytics. After the next input run the day's submissions count increases.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Revoke the API key. The following day stays at zero while the console still accepts samples.

dataSources: `index=cisco_sma sourcetype=cisco:sma:submissions` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Secure Malware Analytics input. The user guide authorizes with a bearer API key, and the compatibility matrix lists `GET /api/v2/search/submissions`. No field list is published, so the search counts submissions.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Secure Malware Analytics input.

description: Counts Cisco Secure Malware Analytics sandbox submissions per day. The add-on writes them as cisco:sma:submissions from GET /api/v2/search/submissions and publishes no threat-score field, so the search counts submissions instead of filtering on a score.
value: A file the sandbox judged malicious can be hunted across mail, web, and endpoints only after the submission record arrives in Splunk. This count shows that feed is still being collected.
implementation: Create the Secure Malware Analytics input with the bearer API key and the host. Chart submissions per day and alert when a weekday is zero.
visualization: Column chart of submissions per day over 14 days.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **No samples submitted** — a day with no files sent to the sandbox is a real zero, not a broken input. Check the console's submission list before paging.

**Suppression:** alert on a weekday zero only when the console shows new submissions.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• A Secure Malware Analytics API key, passed as a bearer token, and the SMA host.
• An index for this data (this page uses `cisco_sma`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Secure Malware Analytics card, and create an input. Set the index to `cisco_sma`.
• The input writes `cisco:sma:submissions`.
• Confirm events arrive: `index=cisco_sma sourcetype="cisco:sma:submissions" | stats count`.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=cisco_sma sourcetype="cisco:sma:submissions" earliest=-7d
| timechart span=1d count as submissions
```

Understanding this SPL
• One event per submission the API returns. The interval on the input controls how often the count can move.
• Threat score and sample hash are not in a published field list, so they are not columns here.

Step 3 — Validate
• In Secure Malware Analytics, open the submissions for the same day and compare the count with this panel.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for Secure Malware Analytics and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• HTTP 401: the bearer API key was revoked or pasted with surrounding spaces.
• The console shows submissions and Splunk does not: the host on the input does not match the SMA cloud or appliance the key belongs to.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We count the files sent to Cisco's malware sandbox each day, so we know those results are still being collected.
